correspondence.excerpt: A Ubiquitous Language is not a repository-wide dictionary, canonical definition registry, glossary file, ontology, programming language, maintenance discipline, or proof of common understanding.
Its generated human view is not an independent source of meaning.
This candidate defines Ubiquitous Language meaning only; it does not admit any context-local language or assert shared meaning across contexts.
Owned expressions used to articulate one exact Bounded Context model.
scope:cyberalchemy-lab-context-metamodel
Repository-wide dictionaries and programming languages.
Unowned glossaries or claims of universal shared understanding.
Governance can define admission while Ontology Lifecycle maps that meaning into event history without owning the admission decision.
Governance and Ontology Lifecycle must own distinct language artifacts; terms such as decision, event, lifecycle, and state cross the boundary only through explicit mappings.
/home/vrondelli/projects/CyberAlchemy-lab
The shared vocabulary used to discuss and build one bounded part of the domain.
The language belongs to exactly one Bounded Context identity at a time.
Cross-context reuse needs an explicit bridge or mapping.
Ambiguity is recorded, not silently collapsed.
UbiquitousLanguage = (id, bounded_context_ref, concept_refs, expression_bindings, relation_bindings, interpretation_rules, usage_surfaces, owner_refs, ambiguity_records, revision_state)
CurrentBinding => BelongsTo(bounded_context_ref)
SharedSpelling does not imply SharedMeaning.

A Ubiquitous Language is the owner-governed set of expressions, concepts, relations, interpretation rules, usage surfaces, ambiguities, and revision routes used to express one Bounded Context's model.
Each load-bearing expression resolves to one current concept disposition within that context or remains explicitly unresolved.
One expression-to-concept binding active in the named context version.
CurrentBinding
Every current expression binding names its context and concept disposition.
Cross-context equal labels are not treated as equal meanings without a map.

Load-bearing expressions have a current binding or explicit unresolved marker exclusively;load-bearing selection and source-owner acceptance of exclusivity are pending.
One concept disposition is distinct from one binding record. Multiple current records with the same expression/disposition satisfy the candidate;CTX01 validator requires unique spelling records.
Language concepts,relations,rules,surfaces,owners,ambiguities and revision routes are separate roles. Accepted set cardinalities and actual owner/revision authority remain pending.
Ambiguity requires an explicit record and does not force every recorded ambiguity to stay unresolved. Actual reconciliation,disposition history and silent-collapse detection require separate maps.
Cross-context reuse and declared meaning equivalence require explicit mapped pairs with exact endpoint contexts;existence of a map marker is not accepted semantic equivalence or authority.
SharedSpelling is label-token equality;the shared-spelling-to-meaning target is outside T. Token normalization,aliases,synonyms and actual cross-context equivalence remain unresolved.

instances.rationale: Same labels can name distinct concepts and multiple records can share one disposition.
